大百货商场必须永续长存。
 The Grand Magasin must be perpetuated.

珍贵之物必须被珍视。
 What is precious must be cherished.

它必须被保存下来。
 It must be conserved.

哪怕要靠所有人的肩膀去支撑，也在所不惜。
 Even if it must be sustained on the shoulders of all.

有人渴望永恒。
 Some wish for eternity.

他们满怀敬畏地吟唱它的名字。
 They sing its name in reverence.

但愿此刻能够永远延续下去。
 Wishing that the now would last forever.

因为它们已被钉牢在原地，好让自己不再动摇。
 Because they are nailed in place, so that they may not waver.

听起来像是一篇郑重其事的悼词，不是吗？
 Sounds like a serious eulogy, doesn't it?

潮流不再来去更迭，这个概念本身也已经过时。
 Trends no longer come and go, its very concept now made obsolete.

这里再也没有季节；过去的季节从未被丢弃，只是层层堆积，化为了沉积岩。
 There are no more seasons here; the seasons of the past remain, undiscarded, ossified into sedimentation.

那就是他们所选择的永恒。
 That is the eternity they have chosen.

那孩子本该从激情之床的子宫中爬出，却在第一声啼哭之前，就已经被哄睡了过去。
 The child, about to crawl out of the womb in the bed of passion, was put to sleep before its first cry.

你无需心怀愧疚，因为它甚至还来不及知道什么是痛苦。
 You need not carry remorse in your heart, for it could not yet have known what pain was.

最后的胭红者死去了，他们心知自己未能守护住新神的诞生——那是他们最后的希望。
 The last of the Rouges died, knowing that they failed to protect the birth of their new God, their last hope.

因他们的灭绝，墙壁变得坚不可摧，再无一丝动摇。
 By their extinction, the walls were made adamant and unshakable.

久而久之，漆黑者们的四肢开始不断伸展，直至化为顶住天花板的立柱，
 In time, the Noirs began to stretch and stretch their limbs until they became pillars pushing against the ceilings,

好让它再也、再也不会动摇分毫。
 that it may never, ever shake again.

看看你眼前的一切。这便是由静止所成就的稳定，再由稳定所成就的保存；
他们将尖钉钉入大百货商场，只为追寻永不改变。
 Look before you. This is preservation realized by cessation realized by stability;
they hammered the nails into the Grand Magasin in search of changelessness.

容我问一句：你认为，他们追求永恒，究竟是想达成什么？
 Let me ask: what do you think they sought to achieve by pursuing eternity?

一个被永远定格在通往永恒的无限收敛点上的人，还能被称作是活着的吗？
 Could a human, who has been immobilized at the infinite convergence into eternity, be said to be alive?

人的一生，不过是一场通往死亡的旅途。无一例外。
 The whole of human life is but a journey toward death. There are no exceptions.

有些人畏惧这必然，于是转而去追求永恒不变。
 Some fear that inevitability, which is why they pursue permanence.

不过，全人类都走在通往死亡的路上，并不代表他们都渴望死亡。至少我不这么认为。
 Now, just because all of humanity is on a journey toward death doesn't mean they desire it. At least that's not what I think.

可正如你此刻所见……等在永恒尽头的，看起来跟死亡也相差无几，不是吗？倘若把这整段历史浓缩成一本小册子，
那看起来或许不过是人类的最后挣扎——他们在追寻死亡的终点，找到了一样几乎与死亡无从分辨的东西。
 But as you are seeing now... what awaits at the end of eternity looks a lot like death, doesn't it? If one were to condense the whole of this history into a small booklet,
it might merely look like the final throes of humanity, which has, at the terminus of their pursuit of death, found something almost indistinguishable from it.

当然，也有人认为"渐近"与"收敛"之间存在着实质的区别，无论二者看起来多么相似。
 Of course, some argue that there is a meaningful difference between "asymptotic" and "convergent," no matter how similar they might appear.

谁知道呢？或许他们是对的。
 And who knows? Maybe they're right.

但人类并没有能力去分辨究竟是渐近，还是收敛。
 But humans don't have the ability to distinguish between what is asymptotic and what is convergent.

这一点，我可以断言。
 That, I can say for certain.

所以在这件事上，那不过是一种没有实际差别的区分。
 So that constitutes a distinction without difference, in this case.

惰性等在保存的尽头，而它的形态，便是死亡。
 Inertness awaits at the end of conservation, and it takes the form of death.

出于对死亡的恐惧，大百货商场停止了一切变化，让自己的悸动沉睡，最终活成了自己所畏惧的模样。
 In fearing death, the Grand Magasin has ceased all changes and put its stirrings to sleep, becoming the very thing it feared.

它拼命地想要将一切所崇拜之物钉牢固定——一切因恐惧而回避、延后的东西……一切它想要守护的珍贵之物……
 It sought desperately to affix all that it worshipped, all that it deferred and avoided out of fear... all the precious things it wanted to protect...

……而为了做到这一点，他们渴望停止一切渴望，最终……死去了。
 ... and to do so, they desired to stop desiring, and eventually... died.

你走过这条路，作何感想？
 How did you feel about this path you've walked?

哦，还有你，经理但丁。我也很好奇你的想法。
 Oh, and you too, Dante the Manager. I'm curious to hear your thoughts as well.

当你走到一条路的尽头时，会选择哪个岔路？
 Which fork in the road will you choose when you reach the terminus of one path?

你会选择尖钉，还是锤子？
 Will you choose a nail, or a hammer?

无论选哪一个，如今的大百货商场都将向内凝聚，在一段几乎与永恒无从分辨的漫长时光之后，化作一棵古树。
 Whichever it may be, the Grand Magasin, as it exists now, will consolidate into itself and, after a time that is almost indistinguishable from eternity passes, become an ancient tree.

这与我曾经见过的那棵世界之树，颇为相似。
 It is much like the tree of the world I once saw.

若那棵树的样貌，在你看来莫名熟悉，那你没有看错。
 If the image of the tree appears oddly familiar to you, then you are not mistaken.

毕竟我们生而为人。心之种与永恒之种，说到底本是同一颗——
这也正是为何，我们绽放出的花，终究都长得如此相似。
 We are born humans, after all. The seed of the heart and the seed of eternity are, ultimately, one and the same—
and that is why all of our blossoms end up looking so similar.
<……"渐近"与"收敛"之间确实存在着实质的区别，无论二者看起来多么相似。> <... There is a meaningful difference between "asymptotic" and "convergent," no matter how similar they might appear.>

只是那并非我们的能力所能分辨。
 Which is not within our abilities to distinguish.

就做一场永恒之梦吧，趁它转瞬即逝之时。
 Dream of eternity, for what fleeting moment it lasts.
